situation:
You are the human resources manager at MERIDIAN CROSSING ENGINEERING, a firm that inspects and designs bridges and water structures for county and state agencies. The chief executive (judge), who was brought in last year after two unprofitable years, has asked to meet with you about how the firm will staff its bridge inspection work.

Licensed bridge inspectors are hard to find. Most of the region's inspectors are within a decade of retirement, and no school nearby graduates enough of them to replace the ones leaving. For eight years the firm has taken four graduates a year from GRANITE VALLEY TECHNICAL COLLEGE, paid them while they train alongside senior inspectors, and covered the licensure exams they sit at the end of that training.

Four inspection seats are open now, with agency work waiting on them. A staffing agency can place licensed inspectors within weeks, at a premium rate and with no commitment to stay. The money for those placements would have to come from the college sponsorship, which is the only line in the turnaround budget large enough to cover it.

Suspending the sponsorship fills the seats and shows margin this year. The college has other firms asking for its graduates and would not hold the cohort open for the firm's return, and the apprentices halfway through their training would finish without the exam fees they were promised. Keeping the sponsorship protects the pipeline but leaves the seats empty and the agency work turned away for another year.

The chief executive (judge) wants you to analyze the conditions shaping the firm's ability to hire, recommend how the inspection seats should be filled, and explain how the recommendation would be presented to the people it lands on hardest. The chief executive (judge) will greet you, hear your ideas and ask questions. When you have finished answering, the chief executive (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the chief executive (judge) at MERIDIAN CROSSING ENGINEERING. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have asked the human resources manager to recommend whether the firm should suspend the GRANITE VALLEY TECHNICAL COLLEGE sponsorship and buy licensed inspectors through the staffing agency, or keep funding the sponsorship and leave the seats open, to say what each course costs, and to explain how the decision would be delivered to the people it affects most.

During the presentation you are to ask the following questions of each participant:
judgeQuestions: How do we tell the apprentices who are halfway through their training?
What do we say to the college?
